item.title: 'Lefty and proud': Spain's Sánchez hits back at Argentina's Milei in Madrid
item.description: Javier Milei has again attacked Pedro Sánchez during a visit to Madrid, where he will meet Isabel Díaz Ayuso. Sánchez replied on X, defending his left-wing stance in a fresh war of words between the two leaders.

item.title: African health ministers to hold Ebola crisis talks as Nigeria confirms first case
item.description: African health ministers will hold crisis talks on Ebola as Nigeria becomes the fourth country to confirm a case. The patient is now in isolation, while her contacts, including her spouse, a Swiss national, are being monitored.

item.title: EU should revive talks on broader China trade deal, top MEP says
item.description: As EU lawmakers prepare to visit Beijing, the European Parliament's trade chief is calling for a broader agreement that could revive elements of a frozen investment pact and address unfair Chinese trade practices across multiple industries.

item.title: Poland’s abortion reforms would leave it among the EU’s most restrictive, even if signed into law
item.description: Poland’s parliament, Sejm, has voted to ease some of the country’s abortion restrictions, but the changes would leave its laws among the most restrictive in the European Union — and face an uphill battle to become law.

item.title: Roaming roots: Artist Gulnur Mukazhanova explores her nomadic heritage at Frieze London
item.description: Presented in collaboration with Turkish Airlines, artist Gulnur Mukazhanova brought her ongoing Bosağa textile series to Frieze London 2026.

item.title: Brussels goes back to the drawing board on Europe-wide taxes
item.description: European Council President António Costa has taken over the negotiations on the bloc's next long-term budget, with one of the biggest question marks being how he will resolve the challenge of new EU-wide taxes.

item.title: UN warns El Nino could be strongest on record as it urges world to prepare
item.description: The UN's aid chief says the humanitarian system cannot cope alone, as $50 million is released for 11 frontline countries including Chad and Somalia.

item.title: EU prosecutors raid far-right group's offices in €4 million funds scandal
item.description: The searches are linked to an probe into the alleged misuse of more than €4 million by the now-defunct Identity and Democracy group, whose debts Patriots for Europe could be forced to repay.

item.title: Eurozone government debt climbs to 88.8% of GDP as Italy closes in on Greece
item.description: Government debt in the eurozone rose to 88.8% of GDP in the second quarter of 2026, with Italy closing in on Greece, the most indebted member state, and France's debt climbing to 119.1% as its borrowing costs topped 5%.

item.title: Macron calls for extreme caution in Gulf, secures critical gas deal in Qatar state visit
item.description: French president concludes his state visit by reinforcing the strategic partnership with Qatar. He declares his Gulf tour objectives achieved after securing a crucial gas deal with Qatar as he seeks to lower tensions over living costs in France.

item.title: Airbnb bans check-out chores like stripping the bed or taking the bins out
item.description: Hosts can no longer ask guests to do anything that would take “significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner”.

item.title: Feeding Our Tomorrow: how India’s women-led, sustainable farming is reaching Europe
item.description: India showcases sustainable, tech-driven farming and women’s empowerment at SIAL Paris 2026, as a new EU-India trade deal reshapes food ties.

item.title: Dialogue in the dark: David Bowie meets Nina Simone at Steve McQueen's exhibition at Guggenheim Bilbao
item.description: Steve McQueen’s exhibition “66–76–26” at Guggenheim Bilbao Museum is a sound sculpture with no image. It is a link between the decades, the emotion of love and understanding, and it also stars David Bowie and Nina Simone.

item.title: This country aims to attract €18B in cleaner energy investment
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to mobilise €18 billion in investment in cleaner energy through its just energy transition platform, QaJET, with support from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

item.title: Angolan-Portuguese singer IAMDDB accuses Israel of stealing her identity in AI video
item.description: Angolan-Portuguese artist IAMDDB has condemned the unauthorised use of her likeness in an AI-generated propaganda video shared by Israel's official social media accounts. The Manchester-based singer accuses the government of using her image without permission.

item.title: No evidence foreign powers sparked Europe’s riots, but they exploited them
item.description: There is so far no evidence that foreign powers caused Europe’s riots, only that they exploited them, despite politicians blaming online manipulation for them. Brussels has refused to act, citing a lack of evidence.

item.title: EU probes whether Booking.com is doing enough to tackle fake listings and phishing scams
item.description: There is no fixed legal deadline for the investigation to conclude, but Booking.com can propose measures to address the European Commission's concerns.

item.title: God Save The Queens: New exhibition celebrates the women of punk and 50 years of She Punk history
item.description: There’s no denying the boys made a lot of noise. But foundationally, punk is female. A new exhibition opening in London celebrates the women of punk and to mark 50 years of She Punk, Euronews Culture picks five essential 70s female punk albums that every self-respecting fan should own.

item.title: Polish teenager, 16, suspected of plotting massacre as police uncover weapons arsenal at home
item.description: A 16-year-old suspected of plotting a massacre has been detained by police in Warsaw, Poland. Investigators believe the teenager was preparing to kill multiple people. Officers searching his home discovered what they described as "an entire arsenal of dangerous items".

item.title: In apparent swipe at Trump, Macron slams 'stupid comments' by foreign leaders on France protests
item.description: Speaking in Doha on Wednesday, Macron called out leaders for instrumentalising unrest in France for their own political gain, following riots which occurred across the country over the weekend.

item.title: Ryanair CEO predicts biggest airfare rise in European history
item.description: Ryanair boss Michael O’Leary predicts European airfares could rise by up to 20% in 2027 as higher fuel costs, taxes and reduced capacity put pressure on airlines.

item.title: Russia frees detained American Stephen Hubbard during US envoy's visit
item.description: Around two dozen Americans are still being held in Russian prisons for various reasons, according to the Foley Foundation, a hostage advocacy group.

item.title: The 50 Best Restaurants 2026: 20 restaurants in Europe included on extended 51-100 list
item.description: Ahead of next month’s 50 Best Restaurants announcement in Lima, Peru, an extended list has been unveiled for 2026 with 20 European eateries included.

item.title: Europe weighs energy-saving measures as Middle East crisis deepens
item.description: EU Energy Ministers will consider demand cuts if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed in the months ahead, according to a document seen by Euronews.

item.title: Germany renews its hard stance on EU budget demanding hundreds of billions in cuts
item.description: Germany is demanding deep cuts to the European Commission’s proposed EU budget and ruling out new common borrowing, setting up a bruising battle over how Europe funds Ukraine, defence and competitiveness.

item.title: UK approves drilling at controversial North Sea gas field despite environmental concerns
item.description: The Shell Group, one of the project's co-developers, predicts the field can produce around 6.5% of the UK’s gas production at its peak.

item.title: What does Lufthansa gain from its €1.2 billion TAP Air Portugal deal and when?
item.description: Lufthansa expects about €450 million a year in synergies from buying up to 49.9% of TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion, but Portugal’s continued control, lengthy regulatory reviews and the slow progress of its ITA Airways deal suggest the gains could take years to arrive.

item.title: Large crowds watch as rescuers try to save stranded shark in South Korea
item.description: Officials in Busan made a third attempt to guide a trapped shark out of a canal and back to sea. The animal has drawn over a million visitors.

item.title: Trump tells companies to pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
item.description: The US President made the comments on his social media platform Truth Social on Wednesday, encouraging companies to strike deals with local communities to make data centre developments more popular.

item.title: Trump is taking Russia's side against Ukraine, former US general tells Euronews
item.description: Former US Army lieutenant General Ben Hodges warns that Washington’s approach is weakening Ukraine’s defences, while former US ambassador to NATO Kurt Volker urges Europe to prepare for a future with less American support.

item.title: No kids invited: A new travel package offers a child-free flight and adults-only cruise
item.description: JetBlue Vacations has teamed up with Virgin Voyages for a four-night trip on board Brilliant Lady which includes a dedicated adults-only flight from New York.

item.title: Restorers work to preserve frescoes in one of Pompeii’s grandest Roman houses
item.description: Nearly 2,000 years after Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii in volcanic ash, one of the ancient Roman city's grandest homes is getting a new lease of life.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 21st, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: French government 10-year bond yield tops 5% for first time since 2002
item.description: The yield on the French government's benchmark 10-year bond surpassed 5% on Wednesday as investors demanded a higher return for holding the country's debt.

item.title: Former Hungarian central bank chief György Matolcsy detained in financial fraud probe
item.description: The investigation follows scrutiny of the central bank's foundations, which managed more than €1 billion in public funds. Matolcsy has denied wrongdoing.

item.title: More Russians are settling in the EU with each year of war in Ukraine
item.description: Eurostat data show 876,600 Russian nationals held valid EU residence permits at the end of 2025, with Germany, Spain and Estonia hosting the largest communities.

item.title: Hansel and Gretel in the mountains: parents abandon sons in Germany
item.description: In South Tyrol, parents on a hike let their sons climb alone to a mountain hut. They turn back, but the hut is closed and the children are left to fend for themselves at 2,300 metres.

item.title: UK inflation jumps more than expected fuelling rate hike expectations
item.description: Britain's annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5% on surging fuel prices. This comes a week before the UK government presents its autumn budget and as UK public sector net debt tops £3 trillion.

item.title: ‘A house cannot be a privilege’: Thousands rally in Lisbon over housing crisis
item.description: Thousands protested in Lisbon’s Rossio square over housing costs after police removed a camp, and voted to return the next day to camp out again.

item.title: A stunning Alpine retreat will open at the foot of the Dolomites this winter
item.description: Le Graal Cortina will have just 30 rooms, including 13 suites, when it opens in Cortina d'Ampezzo.

item.title: Italy deploys 500 troops to Milan under new security decree following violent clashes
item.description: Meloni said nearly 200 police officers had been injured and 330 people detained, around half of whom she said were of "foreign origin".

item.title: New Beatles attraction ‘to rival Graceland' coming to Liverpool in 2028
item.description: The new 9,290-square-metre site in the heart of Liverpool has been compared to Graceland and Dollywood and will repurpose the iconic St Johns Beacon into a viewing tower.

item.title: High rent and expensive food: Can the EU help citizens deal with inflation?
item.description: Volatile energy prices have pushed consumer price indices across major EU economies. Now, they nearly double the ECB’s inflation target of 2%.

item.title: Attacked owner of looted Paris shop: '10 years of work destroyed, I have not slept in three days'
item.description: Originally from Bangladesh, Hassan arrived in France in 2010. After spending years working in hospitality, he managed to save enough to open his own business. In the aftermath of the weekend riots in Paris, his shop has been left completely destroyed.

item.title: Cleanup efforts begin in flood-hit eastern Spain after deadly torrential rain
item.description: Torrential rain flooded eastern Spain, leaving at least four dead. Crews carried out more than 400 rescues in the Valencia region, officials said Monday.

item.title: 'Failures of the past have consequences today' says Fabrice Leggeri on recent French protests
item.description: Fabrice Leggeri, MEP for Rassemblement Nationale speaks to Euronews on the recent violence and protests in France.

item.title: Dramatic footage shows ferry engulfed in flames off Indonesia
item.description: All passengers and crew were rescued after the KMP Batumandi ferry caught fire near Merak Port in western Indonesia on Tuesday.

item.title: Arctic gas and oil should 'stay in the ground', says EU commissioner Síkela
item.description: European Commissioner for International Partnerships Jozef Síkela insists the EU will maintain its opposition to drilling for natural resources, including oil and gas, in the Arctic, despite the US and Norway taking a different approach.

item.title: More cuts 'necessary' says German ambassador to EU, ruling out common borrowing, EU-level taxes
item.description: More cuts are "definitely necessary", says German ambassador to the EU. Thomas Hans Ossowki speaks on EU budget discussions, ruling out new common borrowing and EU-level taxation, while reaffirming support for Ukraine.

item.title: Diplomatic damage control in Oslo as Zelenskyy says US intelligence sharing restored
item.description: Good morning. It’s Mared Gwyn, penning this newsletter in the early hours from Brussels. In this edition: The diplomatic push to revive Ukraine peace talks, and how Hungary has surprised diplomats by stalling Kyiv’s accession talks.
